newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat cuts Feb car worker temporary layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Fiat cuts Feb car worker temporary layoffs.

text.p: Italian car maker Fiat Auto said it would only reduce car production by 3,200 during February, all Alfa Romeo marques, as a car incentive plan will reduce its needs to trim production with temporary layoffs.

The company confirmed to unions on Wednesday that the Italian government's incentive plan to boost car sales had prompted it to reduce worker layoffs and not to trim production back between February 3-28 as much as in previous months.

Only the group's two Alfa Romeo plants will be affected in February. Pomigliano D'Arco, near Naples, will close its Alfa 155 production line for three weeks in February. While the Arese plant, northwest of Milan, will close its production line for the Alfa GTV and Spider for one week.
Worker layoffs at the plants will include 2,600 in the first week, 270 in the second, 2,500 in the third and 3,900 in the fourth week during the four-week period February 3-28.

Fiat had trimmed production by 10,300 vehicles in the January 7 to February 2. The carmaker has for years resorted to temporary layoffs, usually on a month by month basis, to align output to the stagnant state of the domestic car market.

The carmaker, which has a dominant position in Italy's market, is expected to benefit from new government measures announced early this year to give bonuses to motorists who trade in cars over 10-years old for scrapping and buy new models.
